screening_decisions.reason: This is a review article summarizing packing materials and stents in endonasal surgery, not a randomised controlled trial. It does not evaluate steroid-eluting stents specifically.
This is a retrospective review of operative findings at revision surgery, not an RCT. It does not involve steroid-eluting stents or any intervention comparison.
This is a prospective controlled trial comparing revision ESS vs primary ESS outcomes, not an RCT comparing steroid-eluting stents. The intervention is surgery type, not stent type.

This is an RCT but compares levobupivacaine-soaked packs (local anesthetic) vs saline-soaked packs. Levobupivacaine is not a steroid, so this does not meet the selection criteria for steroid-eluting stents.
This is an RCT comparing doxycycline-releasing stents vs placebo stents. Doxycycline is an antibiotic, not a steroid. Therefore this does not meet the selection criteria for steroid-eluting stents.

This is an RCT with steroid-eluting implants, but the intervention is for in-office treatment of recurrent polyposis AFTER ESS, not during FESS surgery. The selection criteria specifies 'undergoing FESS' which means the intervention should be administered at the time of surgery.
This is a cross-sectional epidemiological survey studying prevalence of CRS, not an RCT. It does not involve any intervention or stent comparison.
This is a review article on the pathogenesis of CRS, not an RCT. It does not involve any intervention or stent comparison.

This is an RCT comparing dexamethasone Sinu-Foam spacer (steroid-eluting device) vs placebo Sinu-Foam alone in CRS patients undergoing ESS. Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid, and this meets the selection criteria for steroid-eluting devices in CRS patients undergoing FESS.
This is an RCT but compares lidocaine-soaked packs (local anesthetic) vs saline-soaked packs. Lidocaine is not a steroid, so this does not meet the selection criteria for steroid-eluting stents.
This is an RCT comparing hyaluronic acid nasal dressing vs Merocel packing. Hyaluronic acid is not a steroid, so this does not meet the selection criteria for steroid-eluting stents.
This is a position paper/guideline document, not an RCT. It does not involve any intervention or stent comparison.
This is an RCT comparing gloved vs ungloved Merocel spacers. Neither intervention involves steroid-eluting properties, so this does not meet the selection criteria.
This is an epidemiological prevalence study, not an RCT. It does not involve any intervention or stent comparison.

This is an RCT comparing steroid-releasing implants (mometasone furoate) vs non-drug-releasing implants in CRS patients undergoing bilateral ethmoidectomy (FESS). This meets the selection criteria for steroid-eluting stents in CRS patients undergoing FESS.

This is an RCT comparing triamcinolone-impregnated bioresorbable dressing (steroid-eluting device) vs saline-impregnated dressing in CRS patients with polyposis undergoing bilateral ESS. Triamcinolone is a corticosteroid, and this meets the selection criteria.
This is an RCT comparing glove finger-coated PA pack vs PA pack only. Neither intervention involves steroid-eluting properties, so this does not meet the selection criteria.
This is a prospective review of surgical failure causes, not an RCT. It does not involve any intervention or stent comparison.
This is a review article on the etiology and pathogenesis of CRS, not an RCT. It does not involve any intervention or stent comparison.

This is an RCT comparing triamcinolone-impregnated bioresorbable dressing (steroid-eluting device) vs saline-impregnated dressing in CRS patients with nasal polyps undergoing bilateral ESS. Triamcinolone is a corticosteroid, and this meets the selection criteria.

Study 21 is an RCT but does not involve steroid-eluting sinus stents. The intervention tested is NasoPore (biodegradable synthetic polyurethane foam) vs traditional Merocel spacer - neither is a steroid-eluting stent.
This is a meta-analysis/secondary analysis of 2 RCTs, not a primary RCT itself. While it involves steroid-releasing implants, it does not meet the criterion of being an RCT.
Study 23 is an RCT but does not involve steroid-eluting sinus stents. The intervention tested is hylan B gel (hyaluronic acid gel) for hemostasis, not a steroid-eluting stent.

This RCT uses triamcinolone-impregnated gelatin dressing applied at the olfactory cleft, not a sinus stent. The intervention is a steroid-containing dressing, not a steroid-eluting sinus stent as specified in the review question.
Study 25 is not an RCT - it is a retrospective analysis of 970 endoscopic ethmoidectomies. Does not meet the RCT criterion.

This is an RCT directly comparing steroid-eluting sinus stents with non-steroid-eluting stents in adult CRS patients undergoing FESS. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, appropriate population (adult CRS), appropriate intervention (steroid-eluting stent), appropriate comparator (non-drug-eluting stent).

Study 27 is an RCT but does not involve steroid-eluting sinus stents. The intervention tested is hyaluronan resorbable packing (MeroGel) vs non-resorbable nasal dressing - neither is a steroid-eluting stent.
Study 28 is not an RCT - it is a review/commentary article about outcomes measurement in sinusitis. No intervention comparison.

This is a single-cohort trial (single-arm study) without a control group. It does not compare steroid-eluting stents with any comparator (non-steroid-eluting stents, nasal packing, or no treatment). Does not meet RCT criterion.
Study 30 is an RCT but does not involve steroid-eluting sinus stents. The intervention tested is Merogel (hyaluronic acid pack) vs no packing - neither is a steroid-eluting stent.
Study 31 is an RCT but does not involve steroid-eluting sinus stents. The intervention tested is nonabsorbable packing vs saline irrigation - neither is a steroid-eluting stent.
Study 32 is not an RCT - it is a prevalence survey study using postal questionnaire. No intervention comparison.

This RCT uses triamcinolone-soaked bioabsorbable nasal dressing/packing, not a sinus stent. While it contains steroid, it is a nasal packing/dressing rather than a stent designed to maintain sinus patency.

While this is an RCT involving steroid-eluting spacers, it compares postoperative systemic corticosteroids vs placebo, NOT the stents themselves. All patients received steroid-eluting spacers; the intervention being tested is systemic prednisone, not the stent type.
Study 35 is an RCT but does not involve steroid-eluting sinus stents. The intervention tested is topical tranexamic acid vs phenylephrine alone before FESS - unrelated to steroid-eluting stents.
Study 36 is not an RCT - it is a review article about stents in sinus surgery. No primary data or intervention comparison.
Study 37 is an RCT but does not involve steroid-eluting sinus stents. The intervention tested is HA hydrogel vs CMC viscous foam after ethmoidectomy - neither is a steroid-eluting stent.
